samples.title: The regulation cuts: each at its four steps, on the figure and the doll
samples.about: Your ask of 2026-11-06: "this haircut is not military acceptable, we should have to groom our hair the same way we will have to groom our beards and a soldier with half balding hair would 100% go fully shaved head for service." v0.0.4's horseshoe is gone: the cuts are CAREER §2's seven, men high and tight, low regulation, medium regulation or a shaved head (every thinning man's), women a regulation bun, short, or a braid pinned up. Hair grows 0.40 mm a day on every head, lived or skipped, and each cut is drawn at four steps by its sols since the barber over its due (men 10 sols, women's short 21, bun and braid 42): 0 fresh, 1 growing out (from 0.3), 2 due (from 0.7: the DI says "Haircut's due Thursday."), 3 out of regulation (from 1.0). A man's sides go from skin to a shadow, a dark and the hair's colour, his top a pixel taller at 3; a woman's short cut grows a row at the locks a step; a bun or a braid works stray pixels loose at 3. The game draws them as built until you score them. Each picture is the game's own pixels at 16 px/m (the doll at its own scale), steps left to right, each step facing you, side on and from behind.

samples.title: The rifles as you picked them: the R-7, its finishes, and the designs kept
samples.about: Your scores of 2026-11-08 applied. The R-7 is G2 in the Corps' black with V1's sight ("I would prefer this gun with the scope of the V1, for short and mid range engagements"): G2's skeleton stock, receivers, slotted handguard, angled foregrip, light and brake, with V1's carry handle, its rail and the boxed red dot. A red dot alone is 1×, and the SO-4 has always had its 4× lever, so the SO-4 is drawn as the dot with a 4× flip magnifier behind it (my call, to score): in line with the box when you believe the lever at 4×, swung down beside its mount at 1×; at 300 m its turrets sit on the box. No card draws the green arch any more ("get rid of the green arch it serves no purpose"). The finishes ("multiple colors so we can equip ourselves to camo in environments depending on deployments"): the Corps' black (the issue's), flat dark earth, Mars rust (the regolith's own red dust), Earth desert, Europa ice, Earth woodland and urban grey, one per squad, any design in any of them. samples.title: The stack's figures: two marines in the black suit told apart, moving, in the shoot house (today's look and five candidates)
samples.about: The v0.0.14 reviews: "You and your #2 merge into one blob on the walk" and "In the black suit the legs barely read". The suit stays black (the Corps' armour is black); five ways to keep the two men and their legs apart at 16 px/m, each beside today's look. Every view is the game's own picture of the hall at room 1's door (test-shoothouse at 10:00 on seed 48213: the house's light and floor, the fog of awareness, the post pass, the Mars palette; shot by capture.mjs with the stack moved out), with the stack drawn over it as the stage draws it: the game's figure code (walk cycle B's Combat glide at the low ready, side on with the plant lock; the stack's beat when still), lit by the tint the view gives a figure there, then the post pass's outline, grade and snap. S-h checks that drawing against the game's own picture of GO. The moment, 8.7 s looped: you and your #2 glide (1.23 m/s) from the start mark to the stack on room 1's door, one behind the other along the hall (one depth: the blob), then your #2 crosses in front of you to the door's far side (0.65 m nearer the camera). The gallery's pictures are stills at each tile's telling moment; open a view live (O) and it moves: Space stops and starts it, S slows it to a quarter, the arrows step a tick while stopped, R starts again. Score each candidate in motion; several can be joined (say which).

samples.title: The P-12 on the weapon card: four designs in the Corps' black
samples.about: The P-12 (the sidearm from the Sergeant up, a HAD-17 of ten frangible, the thigh holster) has had no drawing: with the pistol in hand the card still draws the R-7, and the game keeps doing so until you pick. Four designs, each drawn by the game's own weapon card (src/art/pistols.js, reached only by these samples), at three times the rifle's density (432 px/m: the 19.5 cm pistol is 84 px, where at the rifle's 144 it would be 28). What the card shows is what you believe: the slide locked back with the barrel out of its nose; a sliver of brass at the hood's rear when a round is believed chambered (a loaded chamber witness, my call); the HAD-17's rounds seen through a witness slot in the grip's back, from the top (my call: the HAD-17 has its witness holes), "?" on the baseplate when the count was never checked; the well's open mouth with the magazine out; the oversized safety's paddle up for SAFE, down for SEMI; a stovepipe or a double feed in the port once looked at; a magazine in the hand right of the muzzle, its holes to its count. A: the service pistol (squared slide, front and rear serrations, rail, stippled grip). B: the slab (chamfered nose, angled serrations, the RD-1P's cut closed by its cover plate, a ledge rear sight for racking one-handed, hooked guard, flared well, pad on the baseplate). C: the monolith (slide and frame one tone, the slide sloping from a tall rear, a full dust cover, finger grooves, long beavertail). D: the lanyard (rounded nose, fish scales, a window over the barrel, a lanyard loop at the heel: a dropped pistol in free fall leaves). Shown raw, as the hud shows the card.

samples.title: The step panel, three layouts: the core always on screen, the rest grouped by type (rework1)
samples.about: Your ask of 2026-11-11: "If We're going to keep this system of numbered options, we need to find a way to group them by type and find a clever way to make this manageable with top of the head core gameplay options being always visible and accessible (even if grayed out, like hammer if you only have one bullet)." The designer's three layouts of one model: every row in a fixed group and slot (FIRE, DRILL outside a door or inside a room, GUN, BODY, TEAM), the core of five on fixed keys, and a row the situation could offer never removed: greyed, with a badge that says why and points to the fix (→ a keycap: the key that comes first; ▮ and a count: rounds; MKS: the Marksmanship gate; ▲▲ and a rung: not yet taught; a struck silhouette: not issued, the house issues no pistol, charge or flash; a padlock; a struck eye: nothing to act on; ✓ already done, the sample's own mark, my call). Each layout is drawn over the same five true moments, captured from the game by the bots on your seed 1489397426 (the 25 m line on 48213): stepsOf's rows, their times and odds as the panel says them, the believed gun on the weapon card (the stage's own painting, fitted as the HUD fits it), the DI's line; the rows the proposal adds (Stack up and take point, Breach, Flash, Fix, Stop here, the TEAM rows, Transition: pistol) in the state it gives them, with no time where the game has none yet. Each picture is the bottom of the window at its own pixels, STEPS and INSTINCT where the HUD puts them, over a 16 px/m floor with a metre's grid: at 1600 × 900 (--ui 1.25) the verbs in full with their times; at 1024 × 768 (--ui 0.85) one word a key and the times left to the hover, as the proposal has it. Score them here, and in play once the chosen one has its toggle.

groups.title: P3: layout C, "Five that follow the situation": 1 to 5 the situation's five, named, 6 to 0 the core, Tab held for the rest
groups.about: 1 to 5 are a fixed five for each situation, named with its picture at the band's left: AT THE DOOR (Stack up, Stack up and take point, Open, Kick door, Breach), CONTACT (Pair, Hammer, Failure drill, To the head, Challenge: Pair stays on 1 as in Pairs and Bang), STOPPAGE (Gun down: knee, tap, rack; Transition: pistol; Step to cover, clear; REMEDIAL; Cover me), THE TOWER (LOAD, MAKE READY, UNLOAD, SHOW CLEAR, Stop); 6 to 0 the core as in B. Tab held turns STEPS into a fan of the five groups (a half-wheel at its left, inside STEPS, never over the picture): a digit picks the group, a second the row; let go of Tab and it closes. The DI's line names one key at the door: "3". Open view: the fan on DRILL. The designer's lean, 17 of 20; 1.09 presses a choice on the lane (96% in one), 1.13 at a contact, at most 3 from the keys.

samples.title: The walk: today's cycle and three candidates, animated, on the marine in the combat EVA suit with the R-7
samples.about: Your word of 2026-11-11 on the shoot house: "saying that the walking about is goofy is an understatement, the animation is really not there yet." The animation designer's three answers to the chibi's problem (legs of 0.25 m from hip to ankle at a human's speed), beside W0, the cycle v0.0.12 draws. All are the game's own figure code (src/art/figures/cycles.js, not wired into the game), at 16 px/m, in the black combat EVA suit with its carrier and the R-7, at 1 G on the shoot house's slab floor, snapped to the Mars palette as the stage snaps them. Two bands each: the Combat glide at the low ready (1.23 m/s) and Assault aimed (2.03 m/s), the speeds the body walks. Each candidate's frames follow the metres walked in its own steps, and side on its card is placed by the planted foot, so no boot slides (the plant lock: each frame's travel baked in whole pixels); seen from the front or behind the card follows the body, and the slip that leaves is measured and printed. Open a view live (O): Space runs and stops time, S slows it to a quarter, F hides the footprints, R starts again. The questions, with your scores: which cycle reads as a marine in each band (score each); is a bob on the gun line wanted at all in Combat and Assault (B says no); and the front and back views, where the feet slide in every candidate (see W-e's numbers).

groups.title: W: one cycle a view, its frames side on, from the front and from behind, a treadmill leading each row, and two lanes of footprints
groups.about: Each view: the glide (Combat, low ready) then Assault (aimed), each a row side on, a row facing you and a row from behind (the stage's 45° camera makes these the three-quarter views), led by a treadmill (live, the figure walks in place over the floor's moving marks: the camera on the body); then each band walking across the floor, its prints left on the way (the right foot's on the first row, light, the left's below it, dark: each sole where it lay flat, so a clean dash is a foot that held and a long smear one that slid). The line under each band's name: speed, step, steps a second, frames a second; then the slip side on and from the front (px a step), the head's and the muzzle's rows (px, side on). W0's glide is the stroll's four frames at 5.1 steps a second and its Assault the run's four at 2.3 (the legs slower as the body speeds up), both at the low ready even when the sim holds the aim. A, eight frames planted: flat feet, short exact steps (4 and 5 px), the body 1 px down on Down, 4.9 and 6.5 steps a second. B, eight frames rolling: the boot rolls heel to toe, longer steps (6 and 7 px), the head and the muzzle on one row (the turret), 3.3 and 4.6 steps a second. C, six frames bold: three keys a step, the body down a pixel at the passing (5 and 6 px), 3.9 and 5.4 steps a second.
